(top).stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry [-h] {runs,steps,context,receive,agents,check,turn-on} ...

Reads the transcripts Claude Code keeps on this machine and reports the tokens
they record: per background run, per workflow step, and the current context
size of one transcript. Those three reports show no cost, because ka-telemetry
counts tokens and does not price them. It also receives the telemetry Claude
Code can send as OpenTelemetry over HTTP in JSON, writes it to files on this
machine, and reads those files for a per-agent report of tokens, cost and
duration, and for a totals check that holds each session's request costs
against Claude Code's cost metric. Every cost in those two comes from what
Claude Code reported; ka-telemetry never computes a cost from tokens.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

commands:
  {runs,steps,context,receive,agents,check,turn-on}
    runs                tokens used by each background run, and by each run
                        you name by session id
    steps               tokens used by each step of a workflow run
    context             the current context size of one transcript
    receive             receive the telemetry Claude Code sends and write it
                        to files on this machine
    agents              tokens, cost and duration per agent, read from the
                        received telemetry
    check               each session's request costs checked against Claude
                        Code's cost metric
    turn-on             write the keys that make Claude Code send its
                        telemetry to the receiver on this machine into a
                        Claude Code settings file, remove them, or print them
                        for one run

This tool sends no telemetry and makes no network call except the ones the job
you asked for requires.

runs.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry runs [-h] [--agents-json FILE] [--projects-root DIR]
                         [--session SESSION_ID] [--json]

Reports the tokens each background run used, read from its transcript. The
runs are the background runs that `claude agents --json --all` lists, plus
every run you name with --session. Each model's tokens are shown in separate
classes (input, output, thinking, cache_read, cache_write_1h, cache_write_5m)
and never added together. Thinking tokens are part of output, not added to it.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agents-json FILE    read the background runs from FILE, a saved copy of
                        `claude agents --json --all` output (default: run that
                        command)
  --projects-root DIR   the directory that holds Claude Code's transcripts, as
                        <project folder>/<session id>.jsonl (default:
                        ~/.claude/projects)
  --session SESSION_ID  also report the run with this session id, such as a
                        `claude -p` run that `claude agents` does not list;
                        repeat the flag to name more runs
  --json                print the report as JSON instead of a table

steps.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry steps [-h] [--projects-root DIR] [--wf WF_ID] [--json]

Reports the tokens each step of a workflow run used, read from the workflow
run's journal and its agents' transcripts. An agent whose journal entry names
no step is grouped under its agent type and marked [fallback]. Each model's
tokens are shown in separate classes (input, output, thinking, cache_read,
cache_write_1h, cache_write_5m) and never added together. Thinking tokens are
part of output, not added to it.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --projects-root DIR  the directory that holds Claude Code's transcripts;
                       workflow runs are found under <project folder>/<session
                       id>/subagents/workflows/<workflow run id>/ (default:
                       ~/.claude/projects)
  --wf WF_ID           report only the workflow run with this id (default:
                       every workflow run found)
  --json               print the report as JSON instead of a table

context.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry context [-h] [--json] TRANSCRIPT

Reports the current context size of one Claude Code transcript: the input,
cache-read and cache-write tokens of the last response in it, added together.
Output tokens are not part of it.

positional arguments:
  TRANSCRIPT  path to a transcript file, named <session id>.jsonl

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print the result as JSON instead of a line of text

receive.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry receive [-h] --port PORT [--dir DIR] [--host HOST]
                            [--publish-endpoint PATH]

Receives the telemetry Claude Code sends as OpenTelemetry over HTTP in JSON,
on /v1/logs and /v1/metrics, and appends each record as one line to logs.jsonl
or metrics.jsonl in its directory (see --dir). Before writing, it removes
every user.email attribute from what it received, and it changes nothing else
in it. Once it is listening, it prints one line naming the address and the
port it listens on and the directory it writes logs.jsonl and metrics.jsonl
in, and prints nothing more while it serves. It serves until you stop it.
Deleting logs.jsonl or metrics.jsonl removes the records that file holds;
doing so never requires stopping the receiver, and never loses or corrupts a
record being written at the time.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --port PORT           the TCP port to listen on (required); 0 lets the
                        system choose a free port, and --publish-endpoint
                        records which one
  --dir DIR             the directory to write logs.jsonl and metrics.jsonl
                        in, created if it does not exist (default: ~/.ka-
                        telemetry)
  --host HOST           the address to listen on (default: 127.0.0.1,
                        reachable only from this machine). The receiver asks
                        for no authentication and writes any JSON it is sent
                        to /v1/logs or /v1/metrics, so with another address
                        anyone who can reach it can add records to these
                        files.
  --publish-endpoint PATH
                        write http://localhost:PORT to the file PATH, with
                        PORT the port the receiver is actually listening on;
                        without this flag, no file is written

agents.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry agents [-h] [--dir DIR] [--prefix PREFIX]
                           [--where KEY=VALUE] [--compare ATTR A B] [--json]

Reports the tokens, cost and duration of each agent, read from the files the
receiver writes. Each row is one session, workflow run, query source and
agent, highest cost first, with its requests, its models, its cost and the
four token classes (input, output, cache_read, cache_creation), which are
never added together. Every cost in it comes from the cost_usd Claude Code
reported with each request. Under the rows come the Agent-tool agents Claude
Code reported as completed, then the totals check that ka-telemetry check
prints, for the sessions the rows show.

options:
  -h, --help          show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR           the directory the receiver writes to, holding logs.jsonl
                      and metrics.jsonl (default: ~/.ka-telemetry)
  --prefix PREFIX     read every attribute whose key starts with PREFIX and a
                      dot, such as PREFIX.run_id, as one of your labels: rows
                      that differ in a label are shown apart, each row lists
                      its labels, and --compare counts a run as one
                      PREFIX.run_id value, or as one session where a request
                      has none. Without this flag, no attribute is a label.
  --where KEY=VALUE   keep only the requests whose attribute KEY equals VALUE,
                      looked up on the request first and its resource second;
                      repeat the flag to require every pair
  --compare ATTR A B  compare the requests whose attribute ATTR is A with
                      those whose ATTR is B: runs, totals and mean per run for
                      each, then B minus A and B divided by A of the mean cost
                      per run. A request without ATTR counts as having the
                      value None.
  --json              print the report as JSON instead of a table

check.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry check [-h] [--dir DIR] [--json]

Prints the totals check for each session that has at least one request in the
files the receiver writes: the cost_usd Claude Code reported with each
request, added up, against Claude Code's claude_code.cost.usage metric, added
up over every export. A session whose two costs differ by more than 1% of the
request total (of the metric total, when the request total is 0) is marked
MISMATCH >1%, and a session with no data point in that metric is marked no
metric export. Neither is an error: the command exits 0.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR   the directory the receiver writes to, holding logs.jsonl and
              metrics.jsonl (default: ~/.ka-telemetry)
  --json      print the check as JSON instead of a table

turn-on.stdout:
usage: ka-telemetry turn-on [-h] [--settings-file PATH] [--endpoint-file PATH]
                            [--replace] [--remove] [--force] [--print]
                            [--prefix PREFIX] [--label KEY=VALUE]

Writes the five keys that make Claude Code send its telemetry to the receiver
on this machine under env in a Claude Code settings file, removes from it the
ones this command wrote (--remove), or prints them for one run (--print). The
five keys are CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER,
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL and
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. The endpoint is read from the endpoint file (see
--endpoint-file), which ka-telemetry receive --publish-endpoint PATH writes to
PATH. An endpoint not on this machine is not used, and with no endpoint on
this machine the five keys are neither written nor printed. This command
records each key it writes, with the value it wrote, in the same settings file
but outside env: under the first of the top-level keys _ka_telemetry_turn_on,
_ka_telemetry_turn_on_1, _ka_telemetry_turn_on_2 and so on that holds nothing
else. A key counts as written by this command while the record names it and
the key still holds the value recorded. Any other value on the five keys
counts as one you set, including one an earlier version of this command wrote,
which kept no record. A value you already set on one of the five keys is never
overwritten unless you pass --replace, and --remove takes out only what this
command wrote unless you pass --force. A write writes each key that is absent
or was written by this command, leaves each value you set, and says on stdout
which keys it wrote and which it left. --print touches no settings file: it
prints on stdout the JSON that claude --settings accepts, and its notices on
stderr.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --settings-file PATH  the Claude Code settings file to write the five keys
                        into, or with --remove to remove them from; a file
                        that does not exist is created when the keys are
                        written
  --endpoint-file PATH  the file to read the receiver's endpoint from: its
                        first line, an http:// or https:// address on this
                        machine (default: ~/.claude/tools/otel-
                        receiver/endpoint)
  --replace             when writing, overwrite a value you already set on one
                        of the five keys, and record the key as written by
                        this command, so a later --remove takes it out and
                        does not put your value back. A value you set that
                        already equals the one this command writes is left
                        either way.
  --remove              remove the five keys instead of writing them: a key
                        this command wrote is removed, and a key holding a
                        value you set is left and named on stdout. Whenever
                        --remove changes the settings file, it also removes
                        the record.
  --force               with --remove, delete the five keys whatever their
                        values, even with no published endpoint
  --print               print the five keys for one run as the JSON that
                        claude --settings accepts, instead of writing a
                        settings file
  --prefix PREFIX       with --print, the text every label key starts with:
                        PREFIX.run_id, a new random id each time the command
                        runs, is always attached, then PREFIX.instance, the
                        name of the main checkout of the git repository the
                        command runs in, when there is one, then each --label
                        in the order given. Without this flag, no label is
                        attached. Read the labels back with ka-telemetry
                        agents --prefix PREFIX.
  --label KEY=VALUE     with --prefix, attach the label PREFIX.KEY=VALUE to
                        the run; repeat the flag for more labels. A label
                        whose key holds whitespace, a double quote, a comma, a
                        semicolon, a backslash or an = is not attached, and a
                        line on stderr says so. A label with an empty value
                        attaches nothing. A value is carried as typed unless
                        it holds whitespace of any kind, including whitespace
                        outside ASCII, a double quote, a comma, a semicolon, a
                        backslash, an = or a %. Each of those characters is
                        written as % followed by six hexadecimal digits, 0-9
                        and A-F, giving the character's Unicode code point,
                        with zeroes in front to make six: %000020 is a space,
                        %000009 a tab, %00000A a newline, %000022 a double
                        quote, %00002C a comma, %00003B a semicolon, %00005C a
                        backslash, %00003D an = and %000025 a %. So two words
                        is carried as two%000020words, and 50% as 50%000025.
                        To get the typed value back, read the carried value
                        from left to right and replace each % and the six
                        digits after it with the character whose code point
                        they give. Do this once: a % that a replacement
                        produced is not read again.
